News.title: Moment horsemen lash each other with whips as fight breaks out during parade
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment two horsemen brawled on horseback lashing at each other with traditional Argentinian riding whips.

The heated exchange unfolded in front of stunned families who had gathered for the country’s May 25 celebrations.





In wild footage caught by a witness, the pair were seen exchanging heated words before the chaos began.

In just seconds, both men raised their traditional gaucho riding whips and started whacking each other.

The duo were both mounted on horses when the violent tussle began during a patriotic parade, marking the May Revolution.

One rider – seen wearing a white shirt and a black vest – got the first slap of the whip in, before the other man, dressed in black, returned hits.

The man in black began to ride away but the other man followed, not done with the clash.

The pair traded hits back and forth with their horses getting caught in the cross fire.

Both men appeared to be riding away from the witness as the video cuts out, however the argument seemed far from over.

In the background audio of the video, families can be heard shouting, as people attempted to understand what was happening.



Using whips known as rebenques, the weapons were traditionally used by gauchos to handle horses or cattle.

Gauchos are Argentina‘s famous horsemen, similar to cowboys.

They are celebrated as part of the country’s rural folklore for their riding skills, traditional clothing and role in the independence-era cavalry culture.



Local media reported that other riders from the traditionalist groups had attempted to break up the fight by moving their own horses between the two sparring men.

Despite the attempted interventions, the two men continued to aggressively smack at each other, eventually galloping away from the scene.

One witness was heard in the video saying: “They prepare the horses all year for a day like today, May 25, and then they do these things”.

A second person said: “It’s always the same”.

The fight is believed to have started after an argument between the riders from different gaucho groups kicked off over the parade’s marching order.



The clash – which took place in Berazategui, in Buenos Aires Province – happened during the city’s Traditionalist Parade, marking the 1810 political uprising.

Now a national holiday, the day marks the anniversary of the ousting of the Spanish viceroy, which led to the creation of the first local government.

Widely celebrated as the birth of modern Argentina, locals flock to the streets for patriotic parades, folk music, traditional dancing and food.

The shocking ordeal quickly unfolded near Avenida Vergara and Calle 17, where hundreds of families had gathered together for the official celebrations.

Videos of the clash were quickly uploaded to social media, sparking criticism from local residents who had attended the family event.



Neither the Municipality of Berazategui nor local police have released an official statement about the incident.

There were no reports of serious injuries or arrests in the aftermath of the confrontation, according to local media.

Following the violent outburst, the festivities continued uninterrupted.

News.title: Killer Mackenzie Shirilla’s diva demands revealed in jail calls as she begs for iPad and schemes with mom to get famous
News.content:
THE murderer who killed her boyfriend and their friend when she deliberately crashed her car at 100mph made diva-like demands behind bars before she was sentenced, jail calls reviewed by The U.S. Sun reveal.

Mackenzie Shirilla, the focus of Netflix documentary, The Crash, was only 19 when she was handed 15 years to life behind bars for double murder.





She was just 17 when she was the only survivor of the fiery crash, which claimed the lives of her boyfriend, Dominic Russo, and their friend, Davion Flanagan, on July 31, 2022.

A judge described her as “hell on wheels” after prosecutors revealed how the crash was initially believed to be an accident before evidence proved she had previously made threats to kill her boyfriend and never took her foot off the gas.



She pleaded not guilty and alleged she had blacked out and didn’t remember what had happened.

While the world watched her break down in tears in the courtroom during her trial, her attitude in private was polar opposite, prison calls show.

Before she was sentenced and transferred to Ohio Reformatory for Women, where she remains incarcerated, she was held at the Cuyahoga County Jail in Cleveland.

The U.S. Sun obtained dozens of jail calls she made to her mother, Natalie Shirilla, that give a disturbing glimpse at what she cared about most after she killed two people close to her.



Instead of being in tears and discussing the pain the family’s of the victims were feeling, she appeared to be more concerned with technology and how she was coming across in the outside world.

In one audio recording, her mom asked how her daughter slept the night before, and she admitted she was up a lot in the night.

She then said, “I really want my iPad, though,” as her mom questioned when she thought she might get access to it.

“Can you call and ask? Please. Please,” she begged.

Her mom explained when she previously called and asked for something for her daughter she was told it would be special treatment.



She told her, “You’ll get it when you get it.”

A privileged Shirilla, annoyed by the response, responded, “Why the f*** man?”

Calls also revealed she complained about the food at the jail, which she still does to this day, as her ex prison girlfriend, Shyann Topping, told The U.S. Sun she buys her own food with money from family and friends.

As the weeks went by, conversations between Shirilla and her mom went from jailhouse grievances to the media storm brewing outside, and how she could become famous if she walked free.

Her mom, sounding excited, tells her daughter, “Kenzie, it’s on the Today Show.”



A shocked Shirilla shouts, “What?”

Her mom then tells her, “I’m telling you they’re about to get ready for the biggest f***ing plot twist of the century, right?”

Desperate to know how she was being perceived in the media, she asked, “What? What’d they say about me?”

When her mother clarified she wasn’t on The Today Show on the TV, they had covered her case in an online article, she fell silent.

“They’re just reposting the story, but that’s ok, that’s ok right?” she said.



She then told her to start writing her book, adding, “You hear what I’m saying?”

In one of the most unsettling exchanges captured on the jail’s recording system, she openly fantasized about parlaying her double-fatal crash into a Hollywood career.

Shirilla told her mom, “Remember that one guy who got arrested for murder and he became like a model because he was just like… everyone was like loving his mugshot?”

Laughing, her mom responded, “Hell yeah, that was hot. I remember that guy.”

Shirilla then said, “He’s an actor and sh** now. I watched a movie with him in it.”



Her mom, trying to encourage her daughter, then added, “See, now he was arrested for murder, he probably didn’t do anything. That’s messed up.”

Social-media obsessed Shirilla had been growing an online following before her arrest, sharing glam shots of her in designer clothing and smoking weed while driving her car.

And it appeared she still cared a lot about her digital footprint, despite languishing behind bars.

In one phone call, she told her mom, “And please don’t forget to change my Instagram bio. Try and get into that one Instagram account and change my name.”

Her mom replied, “Okay, Kenzie, that may look bad right now. Ok, I’ll put free Kenzie on there but that’s gonna look bad.”



“Alright do hash tag free Kenzie, hashtag innocent,” she demanded.

Shirilla has had multiple appeals denied but The U.S. Sun previously revealed she is not giving up on getting a new trial.

Judge Nancy Margaret Russo previously told the court that she believed the crash was no accident, and video showed that plainly.

“Her actions were controlled, methodical, deliberate, intentional, and purposeful,” she explained.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This was not reckless driving. This was murder.”

News.title: Burnham finds unlikely route to by-election win as ruddy-cheeked posh ‘patriot’ Rupert Lowe spikes Reform’s guns
News.content:
A FEW months ago on this page, I asked if you had ever heard of a chap called Rupert Lowe.

I could hear the scratching of heads from Newcastle to Penzance as you mouthed a collective: “Who dis?”



I went on to explain that he is the independent MP for Great Yarmouth who wants Nigel Farage dead.

Well, not dead dead. Just wiped off the political map dead.

Or at the very least denied the cakewalk to No10 that many pollsters are predicting.



Lowe has some serious beef with Farage after the Reform UK leader kicked him out of the party and set the rozzers on him, claiming he had made physical threats to its then- chairman, Zia Yusuf.

No charges were brought. But Lowe was humiliated and wants vengeance.

Well, time flies when you’re having revenge because the pugnacious Lowe may now be poised to deal a longed-for bloody nose to his old mucker by scuppering Reform’s chances at next month’s Makerfield by-election.

A lot more people know who Rupert Lowe is now.

Because by settling scores with Farage, the former Southampton FC chairman could very well turbocharge the equally vainglorious Andy Burnham into No10.

I know what you’re thinking. How has this ruddy-cheeked posho who is so stinking rich he doesn’t even bother to take his MP’s salary (he donates it to charity) become such an impromptu kingmaker? It is as simple as it was predictable.



To recap: Lowe runs a robustly right-wing — some say “far-right” — political party called Restore Britain.

Restore wants Britain to rewind the clock to a time when everyone left their doors open because there weren’t any Muslims around to stroll in and blow themselves up, or something like that.

Lowe and his growing band of “patriots” dream of a kind of jingoistic theme park experience — England Land, if you will — with Richard the Lionheart its Mickey Mouse.

Mass deportations would be the order of the day, all carried out as ruthlessly as possible.

It certainly has its audience and some of his ideas are hard to disagree with.



But ultimately, it is a pub-chat fantasy that is not just unworkable, it is not very British.

Ordinarily, Restore would be up there with one of those political micro-parties that shriek and holler into the void and then lose their deposit on the night.

Like the Monster Raving Loony Party without the charm.

Yet despite its flaws, Restore is having some success in turning just enough heads to chip away at Reform’s apparent grip on the electorate. It managed to win ten local council seats earlier this month through its offshoot Great Yarmouth First, denying Reform an overall majority in Norfolk. And now it could be on track to disrupt the Makerfield by-election by standing a candidate there.

New polling from the Sunday Times has the ambitious Burnham, with his Oasis playlists and Gallagher eyebrows, winning with 43 per cent of the vote.



Reform and its scandal-hit candidate Robert Kenyon (see elsewhere on this page) are polling second place with 40.

Down the list is Restore’s candidate, local businesswoman Rebecca Shepherd, with seven per cent. Clearly that seven per cent would have most likely plumped for Reform had Lowe not thundered in with his size nine wellies.

Those who dream of England Land are hardly likely to put their X next to a Labour stalwart who, on becoming PM, will turn left faster than Simon Cowell boarding the red-eye to Barbados.



Stripped of its wilder policies and even wilder means to bring them about, Restore is ideologically on the same page as Reform (Lowe thinks Farage’s mob are just too soft).

So meddling Lowe has split the vote and if that plays out on June 18 — and a new poll out yesterday has Restore on an even more incredible 17 per cent — he will have given Burnham a chauffeur-driven passage to No10.

As polling legend Sir John Curtice put it this week: “Restore Britain is making life much more difficult for Reform . . . so far as Andy Burnham is concerned [it] is definitely good news.”

But, hey, at least Lowe will have got his own back on Nigel Farage. That’s what really seems to matter to him, whatever grand statements he spouts about England Land.

It’s no wonder Elon Musk — another disruptor whose No1 priority is himself — has backed him, retweeting him as he breathes on X.



Lowe cannot possibly claim to represent the best interests of the British people if he is prepared to split the Right to the point that it effectively becomes neutered (a Tory/Reform pact seems a long way off, if it ever happens at all).

So if his growing band of followers really do want to save this country, they must ignore Restore Britain and save their vote for someone with a better chance of achieving that.

WHAT A BUTT HEAD I WASN’T expecting to be thinking about Carol Vorderman’s, er, derriere this week. But thanks to a pervy comment from Reform’s “man of the people” candidate for the Makerfield by-election, the twice-winning “Rear Of The Year” is on everyone’s lips. So to speak. Even the snooty Today programme read out the remark that Robert Kenyon, wannabe MP, famously endorsed in all its unedited glory at 7.30am. I nearly choked on my Coco Pops! If you don’t know what I’m talking about, you can find the offending phrase online in all its graphic gruesomeness. I certainly can’t repeat it as if I did, The Sun would have to be reclassified as a “men’s sophisticate” and henceforth only available on the top shelf or as ripped up pages in the bushes at your local park. Anyway, the upshot is that it was an unequivocally vulgar “joke” that even the writers of Viz would have turned down. Polling suggests that Reform fans aren’t too fussed by their man’s history of sexist remarks – he has made a few on X over the years – and as I write, he remains on the candidate list. But once again, Reform UK’s vetting procedures, such as they are, have been found wanting. Meanwhile, Kenyon has made himself look – as one of Countdown Carol’s famous anagram rounds would have it – a complete LRHOEESA.

LOVELY pearl of wisdom from my 12-year-old daughter the other day, who declared: “Life is basically going to Sainsbury’s . . . or going somewhere else.”

She’ll go far.

Revved up over Ferrari . . . but I’m falling short



GAVE the spare-change jar a shake last night to see if I had enough coppers to buy the new Ferrari EV.

Sadly, I’m a few hundred thousand short of the £460,000 needed for this Hot Wheels- looking turquoise tearaway.

Oh well. Might just get an actual penis extension instead.

Far cheaper.

ISLE BE DAMNED GUTTED to have missed the cut for this year’s Love Island. That’s £50 for my pre-audition back, sack n’ crack down the drain. Still, at least I knew what I was getting into, unlike some of this year’s contestants. Like Mica, 21, left, from Barbados, who told us: “I don’t want an egotistical man more into themselves than me.” Hmm. Has she ever watched this show?

GUNNER COST A PACKET



PIERS MORGAN managed to piss off a load of Arsenal fans by attending the Gunners’ last match against Crystal Palace on Sunday then celebrating on the pitch with the players.

How dare he (surely one of the most famous Gooners on the planet) watch his team in action at an away match, denying “real” fans seats, was the charge.

Piers hit back, of course, noting that he simply had the foresight, and funds, to book ahead and fork out a very lumpy three grand (plus VAT) for his four tickets.

It’s called being rich, you see. And there’s a lot of it about among the Arsenal faithful, it seems.

A Gooner pal of mine managed to pick up a ticket to Saturday’s Champions League final for a very modest £70.



Within minutes, she was fielding offers for up to £13,000 for it. And that was small beer.

Someone else, she revealed, had already flogged one for £45,000!

No wonder Fifa can’t shift any England World Cup tickets at top whack.

The high-rollers are blowing all their cash on their local clubs.



EAGLE-eyed readers may have spotted a new addition to the masthead of this page: Columnist Of The Year.

Modesty forbids me to get too overexcited by this accolade handed to me at the Press Awards last week.

Suffice to say it is largely down to you.

This column is nothing without your brilliant letters and feedback. I read and absorb it all – praise, criticism, indifference.

And I thank you for it.



ANOTHER day, another volley of “advice” from Tony Blair to the hopeless Labour Party.

The spiky ex-Prime Minister can’t seem to stop berating Keir Starmer and his sinking ship of fools. Which does make you wonder. Is the leadership race about to get a new candidate?

News.title: Inside Trump’s war on illegal immigration that has cut crossings by 99 PER CENT – so what can UK learn from tactics?
News.content:
FOURTH-generation cattle rancher John Ladd estimates US law enforcement has caught half a million migrants on his land in the past 30 years.

The border between Mexico and the United States forms the southern boundary of his 16,000-acre plot.



For 129 years his family have reared livestock on the land, which has also been the landing site for thousands of illegal migrants trying to sneak into the US.

But since Donald Trump got elected for his second term in 2024, John reckons he hasn’t seen a single one.

He says: “The only relief that we had was Donald Trump’s first term. It pretty much stopped for the four years he was President.

“Then Biden got elected, it started all over again.



“The numbers weren’t as high as before, but they were everywhere — one or two in a group, wearing full camouflage and carpet shoes. It was just out of control.”

Now, despite all the resources, there is still a slow trickle of migrants who manage to cross from Mexico.

Official figures show that since January, 29,890 people have been apprehended at the southern border.

But compared to the 2.14million who were caught in the whole of 2024, the difference is enormous.

The Sun first spoke to John in October that year, when Joe Biden was in office, shortly before the Presidential election that returned Donald Trump to the White House.



Back then, John said migrant border crossings were happening “around the clock”.

Now he recalls how America’s southern border was “pretty much just wide open”, causing a myriad of issues on his ranch.

He says: “The minor problems were they were breaking all my fences and water lines.



“They were stealing everything we owned around the headquarters — cars, trucks, trying to break into your house.

“It was just a daily event, a war zone, of who’s coming around your ranch, into your houses.

“As far as the cattle goes, they were running them everywhere, so the cows were wild and didn’t gain weight like they were supposed to.

“I encountered someone every day, anywhere from four or five to 50 or 60, it was every day you’d find somebody, or they’d find you.”

The difference now, John says, is that there are “consequences for doing something illegal”.



In Trump’s America, the law does not look kindly on those caught sneaking across from Mexico.

The 30ft steel-post fence not only acts as a physical barrier but as a symbol of the tough enforcement which would be coming your way if you managed to scale it.

Border Patrol has stepped up its searches — on horseback, quad bike, and on foot — and now proactively seeks out anyone trying to trek across the desert into the States.

There are AI-powered cameras and drones at key crossing points. Even if you get over the fence, temperatures can reach 49C out in the sun — and Border Patrol agents are ready to swoop on anyone seeking shade in the blistering heat.

Once someone is detained, they are taken to a processing facility where they can be held for 48 hours.



Up to this point, it is not too dissimilar to what happens in the UK.

Here, small-boat migrants are picked up by our Border Force and taken to a processing centre in Manston, Kent, where most claim asylum.

But after two days, migrants who make it to the UK can look forward to a bed in a hotel, or a room in a shared house, paid for by taxpayers.



In the States, migrants will find themselves before a judge, charged with entering the country illegally.

For a first-timer, the offence is classed as a misdemeanour rather than a federal crime — but you can still expect to be deported to somewhere such as Guatemala, or southern Mexico.

US Customs and Border Protection officials tell me that has cut reoffending rates, and these people cannot simply try again the next day.

For those who have been caught a second time, the consequences are far more severe. At a minimum, they can expect a year in a federal prison.

Video of Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents raiding homes, shops and restaurants in search of illegal migrants can be seen around the world, and the message to those wanting to cross the border without documents is clear — turn back.



Supervisory Border Patrol agent Jesus Vasabilvaso monitors the Tucson sector, responsible for 262 miles of the Arizona border with Mexico.

He tells me they now have a nearly 100 per cent prosecution rate for the illegal migrants they catch trying to cross the border. It is this real threat of deportation or jail time that Jesus says is driving down the numbers.

At the peak, in November 2023, CBP data for the area shows they were processing 3,000 people a day who had come into the US.



There was a system of “catch and release”, meaning those people would hand over their details then be granted immigration bail before a hearing at a later date.

In 2024, 43 per cent of those being caught were families and unaccompanied children. Now, with the immediate threat of prison time if an immigrant is caught, the number of crossings is down 99 per cent.

As we visited a section of the border fence near the town of Nogales, Jesus said: “Just three, four years ago, we were looking at hundreds, sometimes even thousands of people crossing the border illegally.

“Now we probably see ten, 20 people a day that cross the border illegally. So that’s a big difference.

“The messaging is that if you come here illegally, the possibility of arrest is going to be certain. If you come illegally, you won’t be able to stay.



“In years past, when we had thousands of people coming illegally into the United States, all we did as agents was processing.

“So we would have women, children, adult males, elderly people, and we had to rapidly try to get them out of the elements because it’s hot.

“We’d try to get them back to our station, try to process them and turn them over to another authority.



“Now we have agents that are actually doing what they’re supposed to be doing. They’re out here patrolling.

“They’re out here in more numbers, out on the border trying to prevent people from crossing illegally.”

Alongside the 3,200 agents like Jesus, Donald Trump has also sent the military into the desert to stop the flow of migrants north.

As we drive along the fence — and the secondary fence beside it — US marines can be seen putting up bladed concertina wire to reinforce it.

Putting up the barrier has cost US taxpayers around $20million (£15million) per mile, and it is still being built.



Trump is currently trying to pass a $70billion (£52billion) bill to fund immigration enforcement agencies, like the bolstered Border Patrol units operating in Arizona.

For rancher John, the costly crackdown is exactly what he voted for.

He says: “They’re scared to death of Trump. That has been the biggest deterrent and why they stopped.

“There’s still a few coming, but I have not seen anybody in person. It’s been absolutely wonderful.”

News.title: Urgent search underway as fears over person’s safety after they ‘went missing in small lake’
News.content:
FIND THEM Urgent search underway as fears over person’s safety after they ‘went missing in small lake’

AN URGENT search has been launched over fears for a person thought to have vanished in a lake.

Police scrambled to the scene this afternoon following concerns for a person in Swanscombe, Kent.





It is thought a young man may have gone missing after entering the water, according to Metro.

Photos from the scene show multiple emergency service workers on a section of shore next to the lake.

There are two small rescue dinghies on the water as part of the extensive search operation.

The search operation is understood to involve Kent Police, specialist water rescue teams, thermal drone operators, volunteers from Kent Search and Rescue and a team from South East Coast Ambulance Service.

A spokesperson for the force confirmed: “Kent Police was called at around 2.51pm on Wednesday 27 May 2026 due to concerns for a person in the Galley Hill Road area of Swanscombe.

“Officers are currently at the scene along with other emergency services.”

Multiple people have sadly disappeared while swimming in bodies of cold water during the heatwave over the past few days.

On Monday, 12-year-old Junior Slater vanished while swimming with friends in the River Ribble, in Lancashire.



Junior’s body was sadly pulled from the water several hours later, Ribble Valley Police confirmed.

Issuing a statement through the force, Junior’s heartbroken family hailed him as the “soul of our lives”.

This comes after eight youngers passed away in separate tragedies after getting into difficulty in water at popular beauty spots in the hot weather.

A 13-year-old boy, two girls and a boy aged 15, a girl aged 16, and another teenage boy were pulled from water over the past few days.

A teenage boy, 17, was also pulled from water at Pickmere Lake, near Northwich, at 4.50pm on Tuesday.

News.title: Brit with ‘extremely severe’ brain injuries Ethan Lacey, 20, taken off life support after Thailand truck fall
News.content:
HOLIDAY TRAGEDY Brit with ‘extremely severe’ brain injuries Ethan Lacey, 20, taken off life support after Thailand truck fall

THE heartbroken family of a 20-year-old Brit backpacker who fell off a truck in Thailand have announced the “devastating decision” to stop his life support.

Ethan Lacey, from Birmingham, was left with catastrophic brain injuries after falling from the vehicle at a busy intersection in the tourist hotspot Pattaya on May 17.





The factory worker’s grandmother, Andrea Chatwin, set up a GoFundMe to cover mounting costs after his travel insurance ran out shortly before the fall.

After 10 days fighting for his life in hospital, Ethan’s family have said they made the heartbreaking decision to remove his life support after consultation with the hospital.

The Thai doctors informed them that Ethan’s brain injuries are “extremely severe” and that he would be left “completely bedridden”.

The appeal continued: “We made the devastating decision to agree to stop all active treatment and move Ethan onto palliative care.



“We were told there would be no quality of life for him, and that he would not be able to breathe on his own.”

But after signing the paperwork for treatment to be withdrawn, the update says that Ethan is “still breathing and his vital stats remain quite stable”.



His family are exploring every available avenue to start medical repatriation, but have been quoted astronomical costs of “around £150,000 or more”.

They added: “We will not give up fighting for our grandson’s life.”

Ethan had taken two months off work for a once-in-a-lifetime trip to Thailand when tragedy struck.

He travelled across the south-east Asian country with his cousin – before heading to the beach city Pattaya alone for a few days.

But a horror accident left the young traveller hospitalised and hooked to life support.



Ethan had been riding on the back of a pick-up truck crossing a busy junction in Pattaya.

Witnesses to the accident said his head hit the ground after falling from the van, before he was possibly hit again by the truck.

Dad Kevin, 40, claims a witness said Ethan was tossed from the moving vehicle during an argument before ending up beneath its back wheels.

The driver allegedly failed to stop and fled the scene, abandoning Ethan in the road.

Kevin told The Sun last week: “It doesn’t seem like he’s going to make it.”



Doctors had warned that Ethan had just “a 30 per cent chance” of survival after suffering three brain bleeds.

Kevin said the family became worried when Ethan stopped replying for three days.

It rang alarm bells as they had spoken “pretty much every other day” up to that point.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Among the last messages the young Brit sent his family was: “I love you.”

Kevin said his son “lights the room up”, adding: “He’s full of life and always having banter with people.”

News.title: Murder probe launched after woman, 53, dies at house as two men and a woman arrested
News.content:
HOME 'MURDER' Murder probe launched after woman, 53, dies at house as two men and a woman arrested

A MURDER probe has been launched after a woman was found dead at a house.

Paramedics were called to a home in Croydon, London, at 9.30am on Wednesday following concerns for the welfare of a woman.



The 53-year-old was pronounced dead at the scene with the cause of death still yet to be confirmed.



Two men and a woman aged between 44 and 69 have been arrested at the scene on suspicion of murder.

Detective Sergeant Suzanne Harris, who is leading the investigation, said: “Our thoughts remain with the victim and her family at this difficult time.

“While we recognise the concern an incident like this will cause, I’d like to reassure locals that we believe this to be an isolated incident.

“Residents can expect to see an increase in police presence over the coming days and must not hesitate to speak to police on the ground if they have any questions or concerns.

“In the meantime, my team and are working at pace to piece together the circumstances surrounding the woman’s death and are asking anyone with information to get in touch as a matter of urgency.”

The Met Police were notified by the London Ambulance Service of the deceased woman at the house on Furze Road in Thornton Heath on May 27.

A post-mortem examination and formal identification is yet to take place.

The force is still continuing its inquiries to locate and notify the woman’s next of kin.



Officers arrested three people at the scene, who remain in custody.

The force is calling for anyone with information to contact it via 101, or anonymously through Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111, quoting reference 2293/27MAY.

News.title: Lotto winning numbers LIVE: National Lottery results for May 27 with £2m jackpot
News.content:
Grandma scoops £1m for family playing late husband’s lottery numbers

A grandma scooped £1 million on the lottery alongside her two children after playing numbers chosen by her late husband years ago.

Retired office manager Rose Tresadern, 80, from near Southend in Essex, said it felt like Derek Tresadern was "still looking out for us".

Former business analyst Mr Tresadern was 83 years old when he died following a short illness last year, not long after the couple celebrated their diamond wedding anniversary.

Mrs Tresadern, together with children Barry Tresadern, 52, and Julie Tresadern, 57, decided to continue playing Mr Tresadern's Lotto numbers every week in their family syndicate.

Their numbers one, four, 12, 15 and 39, and the bonus ball, 48, came up in the draw on April 18 as they matched five main numbers out of six and the bonus ball.

Mrs Tresadern plans to use some of her share of the £1 million winnings to move to a retirement home better suited to her mobility issues, and some on a new ring to remind her of her late husband.

News.title: Iran war live: Trump threatens to 'blow up' Oman over Strait of Hormuz
News.content:
President Donald Trump has said the Iranians 'very much' want to make a deal but 'haven't gotten there', as the US-Israeli war with Iran shows little sign of ending

Donald Trump has threatened to "blow up" the country of Oman - an ally of the US in the Middle East - if it doesn't bow to his wishes around control of the Strait of Hormuz.

The President was speaking at a cabinet meeting earlier today after a reporter asked about a potential short-term deal that would allow for shared control of the key shipping route between Iran and Oman.

He said nobody would control the Strait and added: "It’s international waters, and Oman will behave just like everybody else, or we’ll have to blow them up. They understand that."

Trump also said the Iranians want to make a peace deal but "haven't gotten there". He said: "We're not satisfied with it [a proposed deal] - but we will be. Either that, or we'll have to just finish the job."

The US President's remarks came shortly after the White House rejected Iranian state media reports of a draft interim peace deal between Washington and Tehran.

News.title: Doctors announce NHS strike straight after first meeting with James Murray
News.content:
Doctors announce NHS strike straight after first meeting with James Murray

British Medical Association announces four-day doctors’ strike next month - immediately after first meeting today with new Health Secretary James Murray

View 3 Images Doctors set to walk out again (Image: Andy Commins)

Doctors have announced another NHS strike immediately after their first meeting with the new Health Secretary.

‌



Resident doctors will stage a four-day walkout from June 15 to demand more pay in what will be their 16th strike of the industrial dispute which has dragged on since 2023.

‌



The British Medical Association called the strike after meeting new Health Secretary James Murray today a fortnight after he replaced Wes Streeting in the role but refused to increase the 3.5% pay rise for resident doctors for 2026/27/

‌



Mr Murray said: “I met the BMA Resident Doctors Committee Officers today in the hope of starting a productive relationship and making progress on a deal to improve their members' pay, career prospects and working lives.

View 3 Images New Health Secretary James Murray (Image: Getty Images)

“I'm disappointed that the BMA have refused to consider further discussions about how to strengthen the deal on the table and have instead rushed once again to unnecessary and unreasonable strike action

‌



“I was clear with the BMA that after a 33.4% pay rise for resident doctors over the last four years – the highest anywhere across the public sector – the BMA’s demands for further substantial pay increases this year are unrealistic, unaffordable, and unsustainable.”

The medics formerly known as junior doctors will walk out from 7am on Monday June 15, until 7am on Friday June 19. Thousands more operations will be postponed and more senior doctors as well as nurses will have annual leave cancelled to cover shifts.

The BMA says despite pay rises in recent years resident doctors real-terms pay is still down around a fifth since 2008 according to the retail price index (RPI) measure of inflation. The Government says the overall package of measures that the BMA has just turned down would have led to resident doctors getting an average pay rise of 4.9% this year.

‌



View 3 Images Resident doctors strike leader Jack Fletcher (Image: BMA)

Dr Jack Fletcher, chair of the BMA’s resident doctors committee, said: "We had hoped that a change in leadership at the Department of Health and Social Care would lead to a change in approach. Sadly, we have run up against the same unwillingness to move we encountered under Mr Streeting.

"We were prepared to give Mr Murray time to settle into his role before completing the work his predecessor left unfinished - to both make a fair and meaningful pay offer and make concrete commitments to end the jobs bottleneck throttling the careers of our colleagues. He had a genuine opportunity to break this logjam with fresh energy and ambition.

‌



"He has not taken it. Instead, we are hearing the same tired line: vagueness on new jobs and no further money on the table. We cannot be asked to negotiate in good faith for weeks, only to be told there is nothing left to negotiate about on pay and no further details at this stage on jobs.”

The years-long industrial dispute from doctors started under the previous Conservative government. It has fallen into the inbox of the new Secretary of State after he was appointed by Prime Minister Keir Starmer to replace Wes Streeting, who quit to launch a bid for the Labour leadership. James Murray had previously served as Chief Secretary to the Treasury.

Dr Fletcher added: “If Mr Murray wishes to make a success of his new role, he must confront this issue before any other.

‌



"We are prepared to accept that he may have inherited plans already in motion when he took office. If so, he now has a new opportunity to demonstrate genuine leadership and prevent further strike action. Our ask is straightforward: a credible, meaningful offer comprising concrete new jobs and real progress towards pay restoration.

"Mr Murray arrives in this role directly from the Treasury, where his job was to weigh the costs and benefits of public spending.

“We would expect him, of all people, to understand that the costs of prolonged, avoidable strike action would far outweigh a deal that secured the future of the NHS workforce. The calculation is not a difficult one."

‌



Mr Streeting had initially struck a deal to end strikes by resident doctors during the first months of the Labour Government in 2024, although industrial action by medics resumed in 2025.

The last round of action by resident doctors, which lasted for six days over the Easter holiday, was the 15th strike since 2023. The cumulative cost of the walkouts is estimated to have topped £3 billion.

Resident doctor members of the BMA have a mandate for industrial action until August. The union said further strikes will be announced for July if no progress is made in talks with Mr Murray.

Article continues below

Mr Murray added: “These are simply not grounds for yet more strike action, which patients do not support, puts further pressure on other staff and costs the NHS hundreds of millions of pounds.

“There are record numbers of doctors working in our NHS this year. Waiting lists are down and patient satisfaction is up. I urge the BMA to step back from more damaging strikes and work in partnership with the government for the benefit of their members and the NHS.”

The BMA is also balloting consultants and specialist, associate specialist and specialty (SAS) doctors, in a vote to close on July 6.

News.title: 'Screams heard' near where teen found dead in drain but cops 'never followed up'
News.content:
'Screams heard' near where teen found dead in drain but cops 'never followed up'

The body of 14-year-old schoolboy Noah Donohoe was found in an underground water tunnel in north Belfast almost a week after he went missing while meeting friends

View 5 Images Noah Donohoe (Image: PA)

Police investigating the death of schoolboy Noah Donohoe, whose body was found in a storm drain in Belfast, never followed up on reports of screaming heard near where the teenager was found, an inquest has heard.

‌



Noah, a pupil at St Malachy's College, was 14 when was found dead on June 27 2020 - six days after he left home on his bike to meet two friends in the Cavehill area of the city.

‌



He was found more than 600 metres downstream from where he had last been seen close to a culvert inlet behind houses at Northwood Road in north Belfast. A post-mortem examination found the likely cause of death was drowning.

‌



Jurors at Belfast Coroner's Court were told that police collected statements from only four of the seven residents who reported hearing noises - including screams - between 12 midnight and 3am on June 22, despite having a team of 25 detectives.

View 5 Images The body of the 14-year-old was found in a storm drain in Belfast (Image: PA)

One of the couples, who said they heard three screams at around 1.30am at the back of their house in Northwood Road, were approached by police only 11 months after their initial questionnaire, the inquest heard.

‌



By that point, the elderly pair said they "did not hear any shouting", according to a police notebook entry.

Another resident who reported hearing "something at the front door" and a "letterbox opening and shutting" was never approached by the police for a statement.

A caller to the public appeal told police her daughter heard a scream on June 21 at around 6.25pm at Dunlambert Drive near the culvert, but never gave a statement.

‌



The inquest heard the police logs recorded: "Caller states that her daughter was on above location at Dunlambert Drive end on Sunday evening approx 6.25pm and she heard a loud scream. She did not see anything."

View 5 Images A huge search had been performed to try and find missing Noah (Image: Photopress)

Turning to Detective Chief Inspector McCallum from the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI), Brenda Campbell KC, counsel for Noah's mother Fiona Donohoe, said: "This was information that was felt important enough to be put into a police chronology.

‌



"What I'm interested in is why we do not have a statement from this individual."

In response, the police officer replied: "I was aware that a number of screams were heard in the area."

Ms Campbell replied: "But you have a team of 25-strong detectives, but you come away with only four statements."

‌



According to notes from a morning meeting held by the investigating team, police began using "notebooks and journals" in the case as its log system for information from public appeals had become "unwieldy".

Questioned on Wednesday by Ms Campbell, DCI McCallum said that taking unverifiable statements from the residents who heard screams was not a priority, adding: "It was not going to help us at that time."

View 5 Images Police search a drain during the search for missing Noah Donohoe (Image: PA)

‌



Asked about the urgency around the investigation, DCI McCallum said: "The urgency lessened somewhat when the body had been located. The time Noah was missing was: urgent, urgent, urgent".

Ms Campbell described DCI McCallum's initial hypothesis on June 24 that Noah had sustained a head injury and discarded his personal effects such as his mobile phone, backpack and clothing without any third-party involvement as "problematic".

"Positive evidence at this point in time was that he was a smart, fun, capable boy," she told the long-running inquest, which is now in its 17th week. "By this stage the investigation has his bike, his hoodie and his trainers.

‌



"You were still missing his laptop, bag, contents of his bag. You were still missing his coat. And you were missing his shorts and his underwear, for which there was no explanation. And there is no explanation for where they ended up."

DCI McCallum, who was one of the investigation's senior officers, said: "These were the hypotheses that would have driven the investigation, but that does not mean that we would not have been alive to other information."

View 5 Images CCTV shows Noah leaving home night before he went missing

‌



The inquest also heard that police took 21 months to follow up on a report by a man named as Conor McCaul, who said he saw a person matching Noah's description riding a bike naked in Northwood Road around at around 4pm on June 21 and that a vehicle later came speeding down the street, with two males on board.

"Conor McCaul was not approached for a witness statement until March 2022," Ms Campbell said. "And that's surely a concern." DCI McCallum said: "Yes, I believe that man should have been approached".

Jurors were told that police had secured only one hour's worth of CCTV footage from one camera in Northwood Road.

‌



"I don't think I was aware of that," DCI McCallum said. "In terms of collecting CCTV, I had no involvement in that." He also said police did not ask EE, Noah's mobile provider, to explain why his phone location was different between 7.41pm and 8.10pm on June 21, the day he went missing.

"In other words, the phone was on the move," Ms Campbell said, referencing a report by a telecoms expert which found that "Castleton Park where the phone was found is not within the wedge plotted on the map showing the 1941 hrs ping".

DCI McCallum also said he did not know the schoolboy’s phone had a photo of a stranger's hand, taken on June 21. "This is a real clear line of inquiry that at the very least needs to be eliminated. It needs to be factored in," Ms Campbell said. "The theory that Noah discarded that phone by himself is not a solid one."

Article continues below

DCI McCallum disagreed, adding: "The fact there's a hand does not suggest that Noah's phone was taken away in an adverse way."

The inquest continues.

News.title: 'Every child deserves the opportunity to learn to swim as it is a basic safety net'
News.content:
'Every child deserves the opportunity to learn to swim as it is a basic safety net'

Seven children, including 12-year-old Junior Slater, who was from Clayton-le-Woods, Lancashire, lost their lives in water tragedies over the last few days

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

The growing death toll during this heatwave is horrifying. Children setting out to cool off are not coming home. Families expecting an ordinary summer day are instead being left with unbearable grief that will haunt them forever.

‌



Rivers, lakes and reservoirs may look inviting in soaring temperatures, but open water can kill frighteningly fast. Hidden currents, freezing temperatures, and cold-water shock do not care how hot the weather feels. Warnings must be taken seriously.

‌



But Britain also has to confront an uncomfortable truth. In some of the country’s poorest communities, huge numbers of children leave primary school unable to swim properly. That is not simply a social inequality. It is a national failure with deadly consequences.

‌



Every child deserves the chance to learn how to survive in water. Swimming lessons are not a luxury for the privileged. They are a basic safety net that can mean the difference between life and death.

‌



Blair badly out of touch

Tony Blair may still command attention whenever he speaks about Labour’s future, but this latest intervention sounds badly out of touch with the country many families now live in. For millions of people, Britain’s crisis is not about whether politicians are sufficiently “radical” on AI or deregulation.

It is about stagnant wages, soaring bills, struggling public services and the growing feeling that hard work no longer guarantees security. That is why Andy Burnham strikes a chord when he accuses Mr Blair of failing to understand inequality. Because inequality is no longer some abstract political view.

It now defines modern Britain. Mr Blair is right that Labour needs ideas, ambition and economic growth. But the party is in danger of losing its way the moment it sounds more interested in reassuring billionaires and business elites than in understanding why so many ordinary voters feel abandoned.

Article continues below

Reach for the Moon

As Britain melts through another sticky, sleepless heatwave, the idea of escaping to the Moon suddenly sounds less ridiculous.

NASA says humans could soon live and work there permanently. No traffic, no hosepipe bans and probably fewer people arguing on social media. Tempting, even if the flight may be a nightmare.

News.title: Donkeys stolen and slaughtered to make wellness products sold on Amazon
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Donkeys stolen and slaughtered to make wellness products sold on Amazon

A vile trade sees six million donkeys killed for their hides, which are boiled down to create an unproven 'miracle cure' claimed to help conditions from fertility to insomnia

View 4 Images Dairy farmer and mother-of-five Beth Wambui says her donkey was stolen and slaughtered

Donkeys are being stolen and then slaughtered to be turned into wellness products sold in the UK and around the world, a probe has found.

‌



More than six million are killed each year for their hides, which are boiled down to make ejiao – a gelatine-like substance consumed as bars, powders, or liquids – which claims to treat a myriad of health conditions.

‌



A traditional Chinese medicine, the unproven “miracle cure” is claimed to prevent the effects of ageing, improve fertility and help against anaemia, insomnia, dizziness and even cancer. It is also used in some cosmetics.

‌



Growing global demand has created a booming illegal donkey hide trade in Africa with charity Brooke warning the continent’s donkeys could be entirely wiped out if action is not taken.

View 4 Images Donkeys are being slaughtered to make 'wellness' products, a probe has found

Dr Raphael Kinoti, director of Brooke: Action for Working Horses and Donkeys in East Africa, said: “Everybody who buys these products in the UK and around the world are an accomplice to a trade that is depriving people of their livelihoods.

‌



“You are becoming part of an illegal gang that is stealing donkeys in Africa, pushing tens of thousands of people into abject poverty. You’re depriving women of a critical animal that is helpful to their lives. You’re depriving young men in cities of livelihoods, you’re depriving a young kid of their education.”

Ejiao is sold by third-party sellers in the UK via Amazon and other online retailers. It can be made from skins of donkeys not stolen but which died naturally or were bred for slaughter.

Brooke purchased dozens of ejiao products in the UK on Amazon. Listings include £19 for 100g of ejiao snacks which claim to be “rich in nutrition and contain many vitamins”.

‌



A 250g pack of ejiao powder was £19, while ejiao tea costs £16.58. The UK Food Standards Agency warns products containing ejiao – no matter what the source – should not be allowed into the UK and recommends strict import audits.

Because it is classified as an unregulated and unauthorized product, the FSA advises people not to buy it. Queen Camilla saw the work of Brooke first-hand when she visited a donkey sanctuary in Nairobi, Kenya, in November 2023.

View 4 Images Beth Wambui says her donkey was stolen and slaughtered for its skin

‌



The charity says families in the country are being badly hit by the theft of donkeys. The animals are then bludgeoned with clubs before having their throats slit. Others are skinned alive.

The hides are then stripped and shipped to China – as China’s own donkey population has been all but decimated by the huge demand for ejiao.

Beth Wambui, 50, is a dairy farmer and mother of five from Nyandarua County, Kenya. Her donkey was her lifeline – carrying water, transporting feed and connecting her to farmland miles away. But last year it was stolen and found slaughtered for its skin close by.

‌



View 4 Images Although the African Union made it illegal to slaughter donkeys in the continent, the illegal trade worldwide has led to the deaths of millions of donkeys

Without her donkey, Beth’s income has disappeared. Alongside her community, she is calling for stronger local patrols to protect their animals.

She said: “When my donkey was stolen I felt helpless... like someone had cut off my hands. Right now, I am just struggling, my income is gone.”

Article continues below

The African Union made it illegal to kill donkeys for their skin in 2024 – but the theft and illegal slaughter has led to the deaths of millions.

Dr Kinoti said: “Cruelty like this cannot be ignored. We’re already fighting back against the donkey skin trade, but stopping it will take all of us. Please don’t buy these products.”

Amazon did not respond to requests for comment.

News.title: Father and son make staggering discovery after setting off for fishing trip
News.content:
Father and son make staggering discovery after setting off for fishing trip

Bruna Damaris Sant'Anna da Silva was missing for three days off the coast of Ilhabela, Brazil, after a jet ski on which she and a friend were travelling capsized

View 3 Images Fishermen were able to recover Bruna Damaris Sant'Anna da Silva after she went missing for three days (Image: g1)

A woman who was left adrift at sea for nearly two days was left "confused, cold and asking for water" after she was pulled out into the ocean by a vicious current.

‌



Bruna Damaris Sant'Anna da Silva, 26, disappeared on May 24 while taking a jet ski ride with Dheorge Bernardino, in Ilhabela, an archipelago off the coast of Sao Paolo, in Brazil. Their disappearance triggered a massive search fronted by local emergency services, who are yet to recover Mr Bernardino, and were unable to locate Ms da Silva until she was found in a miracle encounter.

‌



Two fishermen have revealed the shock moment they came upon the desperate woman, a second-year nursing student from São Sebastião, after she had been missing for three days, saying she was gasping for water and heavily wrinkled by the sea.

‌



View 3 Images The woman was found by a father-and-son duo out on a fishing trip (Image: g1)

Speaking to Brazilian publication Rede Vanguarda, father-and-son duo Alex Quintino and Allan de Oliveira Quintino dos Santos said they were flagged down by da Silva while out at sea with their dog Adelaide. The woman, they said, started waving when she saw their boat, and the two pulled her from the sea.

Alex said she appeared confused and cold, and immediately asked the fishermen for water after she was rescued from the sea on Tuesday.

‌



He said: "She asked for water. The first thing we did was get water. We wrapped her in a blanket. Her hands and feet were already wrinkled from being in the water for so long." The family had left aboard their boat, the Quilombo de Caçandoca, in Ubatuba, and had planned to make four fishing trawls before returning home.

View 3 Images The fishermen said they did not regret saving the woman (Image: g1)

Allan had mused before the two left home that it was possible they could find the young woman, and he eventually identified her, approaching with the boat.

‌



The fishermen said they had believed she was carried out to an area far from the coast by a strong current, making it difficult for authorities to find her. Alex said: "The current pulled her way out. If I hadn't found her there, I don't think anyone else would have found her."

The family rushed Ms da Silva to an intensive care unit at the Governador Mário Covas Júnior Municipal Hospital in Ilhabela, which she has since left due to improvement in her condition. Despite ditching a fishing trawl to help the woman return home, neither father nor son said they regret helping her back to dry land.

Alex said: "Saving a life is rewarding. We don't think about tomorrow. God knows what He's doing." Bruna's partner, Beatriz Luz, told Rede Vanguarda the woman disappeared while travelling to a gathering held on a speedboat.

Article continues below

She added that she had never ridden a jet ski before she disappeared alongside Mr Bernardino, who remains missing after the two capsized last week.

News.title: Fifa ordered to explain World Cup ticket pricing
News.content:
Fifa must answer questions after allegations of "artificially inflating prices" and "misleading fans" over the sale of tickets for the 2026 World Cup.

It comes as the attorneys general of New York and New Jersey officially launched an investigation into Fifa's practices.

New Jersey attorney general Jennifer Davenport called the process a "gauntlet of confusion, fake scarcity and impossibly high prices".

She added there would be a "thorough investigation of Fifa's conduct" with world football's governing body subpoenaed to provide information.

A subpoena compels a party to release specified internal documents or information.

Davenport made a joint announcement alongside New York attorney general Letitia James and the New York City department of consumer and worker protection (DCWP).

DCWP commissioner Samuel AA Levine said the body would be taking "allegations of blatantly deceptive conduct very seriously" and would look into allegations of "artificially inflating prices".

In particular, Fifa has been asked to explain why tickets have "exceeded the prices for any previous World Cup tournament".

Fans have reported they were "misled" about the location of seats, including through the creation of more expensive 'front' category tickets released after the initial sales.

It is also alleged variable pricing through various phases had allowed Fifa to raise prices for about 90 of the 104 fixtures by an average of 34%.

The investigation will consider how the ticket release schedule and public statements may have impacted prices.

Fifa has declined to comment.

Guzman y Gomez, an Australia-based Mexican restaurant chain that once planned a major expansion across the United States, has abruptly closed all of its American locations.

Founder and CEO Steven Marks told Business News Australia Friday that the company ultimately determined the U.S. business was not generating strong enough returns to justify continued investment, prompting an immediate exit and the closure of its eight Chicago-area restaurants.

“I have always been confident in the differentiation of our food and guest experience, this was not translating to an improvement in sales momentum,” Marks said. He added, “Having spent the last three months in the U.S., I realized this was going to take significantly more time and capital than we had expected.”

The chain launched its U.S. operations in 2020 with plans to build a nationwide presence that could eventually grow to hundreds of restaurants. Instead, it opened just eight locations, all in the Chicago area, including Bucktown, Schaumburg, Evanston, Crystal Lake, Deerfield, Buffalo Grove and Des Plaines, where it tested its menu of burritos, tacos, nachos, quesadillas, enchiladas and breakfast burritos.

“In assessing the trajectory of the current network, the board and I have concluded that the business is unlikely to deliver the performance that would justify continued investment of shareholder capital,” Marks said.

open image in gallery All eight Guzman y Gomez restaurants in the Chicago area have permanently closed after the company determined its US operations were not generating strong enough returns to justify continued investment ( Getty )

open image in gallery The U.S. shutdowns were effective May 22 ( Getty )

The Guzman y Gomez website states the U.S. shutdown was effective May 22.

“To every guest who came through our doors - you chose us, and we never took that for granted. To our team - thank you. Your passion and your purpose built something special,” the website reads.

It also invited customers to the restaurant’s more than 260 international locations.

“If you're ever in Australia, Singapore or Japan, come find us - we'll have your favs waiting for you,” restaurant officials wrote.

News.content:

A roster of A-list celebrities has been invited to attend President Donald Trump’s UFC event at the White House next month, according to a new report.

The six bouts, set to take place in an octagon and under towering lighting rigs on the South Lawn, will be held on June 14 in honor of America’s 250th birthday — though the date also coincides with Trump’s 80th birthday.

UFC CEO Dana White has extended invitations to former New England Patriots quarterback Tom Brady and actor-wrestler Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson, Time reported. Movie stars Adam Sandler, Jared Leto and Jason Statham have also been offered tickets, alongside film director Guy Ritchie and “Access Hollywood” host Mario Lopez.

Many of these individuals — whose attendance has not been confirmed — are avid aficionados of the UFC, a sport largely popular with young men. Brady has listed his favorite fighters during an interview; Leto has shared posts about upcoming bouts.

open image in gallery Former Patriots quarterback Tom Brady has been invited to attend the June 14 White House UFC event, Time reported ( Getty Images for OBB Media - FAN )

open image in gallery Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson, a blockbuster action star and wrestler, also received an invite ( Getty Images )

In 2011, Statham told an interviewer he has “always been a fan.” He added: “They're the ultimate athlete. They just have so much concentration and mental strength. They overcome their fears and they're the true gladiators.”

When reached by The Independent, the White House declined to comment. The Independent has contacted the UFC for comment.

The June 14 event, dubbed UFC Freedom 250, will feature about 4,300 seats around the octagon. At least 1,200 of them will be reserved for active duty service members, Time reported.

All seats are expected to be invite-only, though members of the public can apply for free tickets to watch the fights from the Ellipse, a sprawling park located next to the White House.

“We’re gonna give away about 85,000 tickets [to the Ellipse],” White said earlier this month. “There’s a process, you have to register for tickets, and they’re free…Literally, you’ll be able to see the fight[s] from the Ellipse, but we have screens, we’ve got stages, we’ve got music.”

open image in gallery This week, cranes were seen assembled massive lighting rigs on the South Lawn in preparation for the UFC event ( Getty )

Construction for the event kicked off this week, with photos showing cranes assembling massive lighting rigs that appear to be nearly as tall as the executive mansion. Earlier this month, Trump showed off a nighttime rendering of the octagon surrounded by stars and stripes decor.

“This will be the greatest show on earth,” the 79-year-old president told reporters. “These are real warriors. When we talk about warriors, these are warriors.”

White, who is friends with Trump, told Time that the White House fighting extravaganza is “not at all” intended to be political.

That hasn’t stopped Democrats from railing against the upcoming spectacle.

“Trump is building a golden ballroom and for his birthday party — arranging a UFC fight on the White House grounds — while you’re fighting to pay this month’s bills. Could he be more out of touch?” Senator Adam Schiff, a California Democrat, wrote on X.

open image in gallery Earlier this month, the 79-year-old president showed off renderings of the octagan, which is seen surrounded by stars and stripes ( AFP/Getty )

Trump himself has long been an avid UFC fan, frequently appearing cageside at major fights. In 2019, he made history as the first sitting president to attend an event. Last month, he attended UFC 327 in Miami alongside Secretary of State Marco Rubio — while peace talks to end the Iran war collapsed in Pakistan.

While there, he joked that an athlete was too attractive to step into the ring, while also questioning his own potential as a fighter.

“You could be a model,” Trump told Brazilian fighter Paolo Costa. “You’re too good looking to be a fighter.”

Elsewhere, while watching welterweight Kevin Holland and speaking to White, the president asked: “Now if I wanted to heavy train, because I’m a very good athlete, could I beat the s*** out of him? Or would you stop me from trying?”

“I would stop you, sir,” White replied, according to Time.

YouTube is rolling out more prominent AI disclosure labels and a new detection system designed to automatically identify AI-generated or AI-edited content as it becomes increasingly difficult to distinguish what’s real.

Creators will still be required to disclose when they use AI, but YouTube is adding automated tools that can flag “significant photorealistic AI use,” YouTube announced in a blog post Wednesday. Starting this month, if a creator fails to properly label a video, the platform may apply the disclosure automatically based on its detection systems.

If a video is incorrectly labeled, creators will be able to adjust the disclosure through YouTube Studio. However, YouTube says some AI labels will be permanent, including content created with its own generative AI tools such as Veo or Dream Screen, as well as videos that contain C2PA metadata indicating they were fully generated by AI.

“We’ve heard consistently from our community that they value transparency when it comes to generative AI content,” YouTube’s blog post states. “These changes are designed to balance transparency with creator control.”

The change comes as more and more AI is being used online. It has led some users to complain that distinguishing between real and fake videos online have become harder. That has led to calls for more transparency by media companies to clearly label AI videos.

open image in gallery For long-form videos, the AI label will appear beneath the player, while on YouTube Shorts, it will appear as an on-screen overlay during playback ( Getty Images )

open image in gallery YouTube released this image Wednesday of what the AI disclosure labels will look like on videos and Shorts ( YouTube )

The platform is also changing where those labels appear. For long-form videos, the AI tag will now sit directly beneath the video player, while on YouTube Shorts, it will show up as a visible overlay during playback.

“The goal here is context at a glance. If it looks real but was made with AI, viewers will know immediately,” Rene Ritchie, YouTube head of editorial and creator liaison, said in a video about the changes.

Ritchie added that the AI labels alone “do not affect how our videos are recommended or whether they can earn money. This is purely about giving viewers the right information at the right time.”

Meanwhile, YouTube is taking a lighter approach to content that is only partially AI-influenced. Videos labeled as “unrealistic, animated or slightly altered,” rather than fully AI-generated, will still get an AI disclosure, but it will appear in the expanded description instead of as a more prominent on-screen label.

The changes follow YouTube’s March move to expand its likeness-detection program to all creators aged 18 and older. That tool is designed to help users detect and manage how AI is used to represent their likeness on the platform.

Once enrolled, creators can receive alerts when YouTube’s systems detect videos that may use synthetic or altered versions of their face. They can then review the content and request removal of unauthorized videos directly through YouTube Studio.

CBS News declined to renew the contract of 60 Minutes correspondent Sharyn Alfonsi months after her public feud with the network’s editor-in-chief, Bari Weiss.

Alfonsi, who publicly clashed with Weiss after her segment on El Salvador’s notorious CECOT prison was abruptly pulled off the air in December, confirmed her deal expired on Saturday to The New York Times.

Efforts by Alfonsi’s agent to get CBS to discuss a new contract were met with “absolute silence from network executives,” she said in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter.

“The message could not be clearer: my time at 60 Minutes is apparently over,” she reportedly said.

“In the coming days, network leadership may attempt to hide behind corporate euphemisms like ‘modernization’ and ‘restructuring’ to explain away my departure. Don’t be misled. This was not a routine corporate transition; it was a deliberate choice to penalize a journalist for refusing to sanitize factually accurate reporting, and it sends a chilling message to the entire newsroom.”

open image in gallery 60 Minutes correspondent Sharyn Alfonsi says CBS has declined to renew her contract, months after she and editor-in-chief Bari Weiss got into a public feud over her segment ( 60 Minutes/CBS News )

Alfonsi’s statement continued: “Fearless, independent reporting has always been the defining standard at 60 Minutes. Today CBS management is abandoning that mission, choosing access journalism over accountability and protecting power rather than scrutinizing it. The wall between editorial independence and corporate interest at CBS is being methodically torn down. Journalists willing to challenge authority are being pushed aside in favor of those who will not. If this continues, the result will be a broadcast that looks like 60 Minutes but lacks the courage and character to produce journalism that matters.”

The longtime correspondent went on to thank her colleagues “who became family — working beside you has been the privilege of a lifetime. You are second to none. I’ve learned exactly what it costs to hold the line right now. Hold it anyway. Viewers and the people who trust us with their stories deserve nothing less.”

Alfonsi remains employed at CBS, but told the NYT that she did not expect to return to 60 Minutes.

“I’m not resigning,” she said. “If they want me gone because I did my job, they’ll have to fire me.”

The Independent has contacted Alfonsi and CBS News for comment.

open image in gallery Weiss was hired as editor-in-chief of CBS after Skydance Media bought CBS’ parent company, Paramont Global, in August ( Getty )

60 Minutes ultimately aired Alfonsi’s segment in January, a month later than expected. Weiss claimed it was “not ready” to air in December due to the lack of on-the-record comments from the Trump administration. She had also suggested several late editorial changes, the NYT reports.

At the time, Alfonsi fumed in a memo to her colleagues that Weiss’ decision to spike the segment appeared to be politically motivated.

“Our story was screened five times and cleared by both CBS attorneys and Standards and Practices,” she wrote, the NYT reports. “It is factually correct. In my view, pulling it now — after every rigorous internal check has been met is not an editorial decision, it is a political one.”

Alfonsi also noted that if the White House’s “refusal to participate becomes a valid reason to spike a story, we have effectively handed them a ‘kill switch’ for any reporting they find inconvenient.”

Alfonsi spoke about the experience during an April 30 speech at the National Press Club in Washington, after she received a Ridenhour Courage Prize for “life-long defense of the public interest and passionate commitment to social justice.”

open image in gallery ( Getty )

“I will not linger on the internal mechanics of the dust-up at CBS that led to our CECOT story being pulled, but we have to be honest about what it represents,” she said, according to The Guardian.

“It wasn’t an isolated editorial argument. In my view, it was the result of a more aggressive contagion: the spread of corporate meddling and editorial fear. It’s hard to watch.”

Alfonsi also said that “corporate calculations” were affecting journalism, saying, “Some executives are asking not, ‘Is the story true?’ but, ‘Is it good for business?’”

Weiss was hired as editor-in-chief by David Ellison, son of billionaire and Republican mega-donor Larry Ellison, after his company, Skydance Media, bought CBS’s parent company, Paramount Global, for $8 billion in August.

During negotiations of that deal, Paramount paid President Donald Trump $16 million to settle a lawsuit over his claim that 60 Minutes unfairly edited an interview in 2024 with Kamala Harris.

Weiss has been accused by critics of being too Trump-friendly. Most recently, the network has faced backlash over its handling of the Iran war, with some CBS staffers claiming the network is carrying out a “propaganda-palooza” on behalf of the Trump administration’s military campaign, according to Zeteo.

As immigrant detainees inside a two-story detention center enter the sixth day of a hunger strike to protest conditions inside the facility, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin dismissed their complaints and chalked up their actions to a lack of “ethnic food."

“They’re refusing to eat because they want their ethnic food,” he said during a meeting with President Donald Trump’s Cabinet on Wednesday.

“Well, they can go back to their country and get whatever food they want,” he said. “We’re giving them the calories they want. This isn’t Holiday Inn.”

Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers in military gear with heavily armored police trucks continues to stand off against protesters at the Delaney Hall detention center in Newark, New Jersey, where demonstrators have rallied for days to support striking detainees inside.

“These aren’t protesters. These people are fake. They’re all paid for,” Trump said Wednesday. “We run the finest facilities anywhere in the world of their type. … There’s nobody that runs a facility like we do.”

open image in gallery DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin has disputed reports of detainees on hunger strike inside a sprawling immigration detention center in New Jersey, where protesters have rallied outside for several days to bring attention to conditions inside the facility ( Reuters )

Two people were arrested late Tuesday during another night of clashes between ICE agents and demonstrators who say officers deployed pepper spray into the crowds.

Mullin announced on X that two “anti-ICE rioters” were arrested on charges of assaulting, resisting and impeding federal officers, and warned that “anyone who assaults law enforcement will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law.”

Roughly 300 people have been on a hunger and labor strike since May 22 to protest conditions inside Delaney Hall, where detainees and members of Congress who visited them have alleged unconstitutional and inhumane conditions, including rotting food, due process violations, a lack of access to legal counsel and retaliation from ICE agents for their ongoing strike actions.

“We feel vulnerable and, in a way, kidnapped — detained without justification — not to mention that we are being tortured physically and psychologically due to the poor food resources provided in these detention centers,” detainees wrote in a letter shared by attorneys last week.

They signed the letter “S.O.S.”

New Jersey Sen. Andy Kim, among several lawmakers who visited the facility in recent days, was hit by chemical agents on Monday night after ICE agents fired pepper spray and pepper balls into a crowd of protesters.

Mullin said he shouldn’t have been there.

“You have one of the senators complained because he got splattered with a pepper ball,” Mullin said Wednesday. “I’m sorry, you probably shouldn’t have been there.”

open image in gallery ICE agents fired pepper spray at protesters during an ongoing standoff outside the detention center, where two people were arrested during volatile clashes May 26 ( Reuters )

open image in gallery Gabriella Soto, whose husband is on a hunger strike, speaks out against conditions at Delaney Hall alongside New York Democratic Rep. Adriano Espaillat (right) after the congressman toured the facility May 27 ( Getty )

After the incident, Kim said ICE sent in an armored vehicle and armed agents who only “poured gasoline on the fire” instead of speaking with him about conditions at the jail.

“Delaney Hall is a failure; it’s this administration’s failure,” he wrote. “The only way to make this right for our communities is to shut it down and make sure the failures we’ve seen never happen again.”

Kim’s fellow New Jersey Sen. Cory Booker called the detention center a “moral assault” on the state.

“It should close and should never have opened in the first place,” he wrote. “A private, for-profit detention facility should never be allowed to profit from the pain and fear of vulnerable human beings.”

The 1,000-bed, two-story facility opened May 1, 2025 and is operated by private prison contractor GEO Group, which was awarded a 15-year, $1 billion contract to run it.

The strike and ongoing protests follow urgent demands from immigrants, lawyers and members of Congress to address the growing populations in similar prison-like facilities, which are facing an avalanche of lawsuits over conditions inside them.

The Trump administration is expecting to deport at least 1 million people a year and hold as many as hold at least 99,000 immigrants in detention on any given day, according to ICE.
